label: July 1915
headline: Liquid Fire at Hooge
deck: Flamethrowers strike the British line; South-West Africa surrenders
caption: Jets of burning oil arc over a shattered breastwork near Hooge
body: Before dawn on 30 July, at Hooge, east of Ypres, German pioneers turn a new weapon on the British trenches: jets of burning oil thrown across the parapet. The defenders, young soldiers of the New Army, fall back several hundred yards before they can rally.

In Africa, on 9 July, the German forces of South-West Africa lay down their arms to General Botha at Khorab. A South African army has marched across the desert to take the colony in a campaign of a few months.

On the Isonzo the Italians open their second offensive on 18 July and fight for the stony Carso plateau above the river. They gain a few hills at great cost; the Austro-Hungarian line bends but holds.
In the east the Austro-German armies close on Warsaw from the north and the south, and the Russians prepare to give up the city.
briefs: Washington sends Berlin a third, sterner note over the Lusitania
British and Indian troops take Nasiriyah on the Euphrates
Britain begins a national register of men and women aged 15 to 65
